children: Michael Burry (Trades, Portfolio) still likes Veeva Systems Inc. (VEEV, Financials) as a software play even after he just decreased his position in Big Short investor Michael Burry (Trades, Portfolio)'s portfolio. Burry revealed a holding in Veeva in April as part of his software-rebound theory, then upped his position in May.

He said the recent trim was not a change in his larger optimistic perspective, but a reflection of the stock's strong advance to a major resistance level and a higher valuation. Snowflake Inc. (SNOW, Financials) is another story.

The stock was very overvalued, Burry said, and he pointed to longer-term problems for the corporation as businesses increasingly keep sensitive data in-house as AI and quantum computing improve. The warning is coming at an odd moment.
Snowflake stock soared more than 23% in premarket trade as the firm topped Wall Street estimates and lifted its fiscal 2027 product revenue outlook.

The business now sees product revenue of $6.07 billion, up 36% year over year, vs earlier expectations of $5.84 billion and 31% growth. Snowflake has a market cap of approximately $110.84 billion. Investors can see the difference.

Burry has taken some profits in Veeva but still sees potential there, while believing Snowflake's robust growth doesn't warrant its pricing. The next question is whether Snowflake can keep growing faster for long enough to prove that warning false.

title: Michael Burry Calls Snowflake Overvalued as Shares Jump 23%
